analyst_view.overall: Werder Bremen (6th, 18 points, unbeaten in five home games) host bottom side Gladbach (4 points from 10, one point from their last three games) on Friday night, coming off a 4-0 Nordderby win over Hamburg and a contract extension for coach Daniel Thioune. For Werder, Mitchell Weiser trained normally on Monday and Thioune expects him to be available, while Marco Grull, their best assist provider, has a calf problem and would be a bench option at most; Felix Agu is too early, and Stage, Musah and Topp stay out. For Gladbach, Sports Mole reports Tim Kleindienst is ruled out, Hugo Bolin is back in training but Alexander Blessin says he will not rush anyone, and Robin Hack missed Tuesday's training with a muscle problem and is listed as doubtful. The numbers already take off Weiser, Bolin and Ullrich and add for Werder's strong recent shooting and Gladbach's high card count, but they do not know about Grull's absence or Hack's doubt, so I trim goals and shots on target slightly. No referee has been named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals, 1.9 for Werder, and already take off Weiser (who now looks likely to play, a small plus) and Bolin and Ullrich for Gladbach. What they do not see is that Grull, Werder's top creator, is at best a substitute, and that Hack, one of Gladbach's few attacking threats, is doubtful with a muscle problem while Kleindienst is still not ready. Together that pulls a little lower, to about 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, 5.4 for Werder. Weiser's likely return gives Werder their usual width on the right, but Grull's absence and Agu still being out on the left take some crossing away; Gladbach's recent habit of conceding corners is already counted. These balance out, so I stay at about 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. Gladbach have collected 20 cards in their last six games, the sign of a side scrapping at the bottom, and the numbers already add about 8% for that; Werder's own card count has been low. No referee has been named and there is no derby edge, so I stay at about 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.4 shots, 18.3 for Werder. Werder's 105 shots in six games are already counted with an 11% boost, and Fullkrug leading the line in good scoring form is part of that; Gladbach have lost five of seven away games and will likely sit deep. Grull and Hack missing would cost a few shots, Weiser returning adds some, so I stay at about 31.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.2 shots on target, 7.0 for Werder, already boosted by Werder's sharp recent finishing (Njinmah scored twice against Hamburg). With Grull out of the starting side and Hack doubtful for a Gladbach attack already without Kleindienst, I take a little off, to about 11.0.
